newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Commerce chief orders tighter security.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Commerce chief orders tighter security.

text.p: Commerce Secretary William Daley has ordered more limited access to classified information following allegations that a former employee passed such data to the Asian company where he used to work, the department said on Wednesday.

A memo released by the department said the number of people who receive security clearances will be limited and the department will take steps to make sure that granting security clearances does not become routine. New security measures that went into effect on Tuesday also call for stricter protection of classified information and enhancing security reviews of departing employees.

The new guidelines followed allegations that John Huang, a central figure in the Democratic fund-raising scandal, passed classified information to his previous employer, Indonesian-based Lippo Group, while he was a Commerce Department official. He left the department in 1995 to become a Democratic Party fund-raiser.

His activities as a fund-raiser and connections to Asian business have been a major focus of investigations into the scandal that has forced the Democratic Party to return more than $1 million in possibly illegal contributions.
A Senate committee is set to begin hearings on the fund-raising scandal and Huang's activities next week.
